oliver: Quick sanity check — after the hotfix this morning I'm still seeing a couple of double-free traces when demoting prefixes under pressure. Repro'd on canary at ~30% mem with bursty writes. Anyone seen the same? :eyes:

sam: Yep, saw it once during the perf run. Stack trace points at demotePath -> releaseLease -> demoteCallback being invoked twice. I suspect a race between eviction and handoff retry.

maria: I reproduced locally with a tight loop: create prefix, write hot keys, trigger demote, then concurrently call handoff. I pulled a short log: 
```
I2026-02-11T15:02:03 demote: prefix=tenant/42 epoch=102 fence=0xdeadbeef
I2026-02-11T15:02:03 handoff: start prefix=tenant/42 epoch=102
I2026-02-11T15:02:03 demote: callback invoked for prefix=tenant/42
I2026-02-11T15:02:03 demote: callback invoked for prefix=tenant/42
```
No obvious nullptrs, just two callbacks.

nora: My hypothesis: we don't have a single canonical invariants check that ensures 'demoteCallback' is only scheduled once per demote token. We maintain token ownership and an epoch, but the callback scheduling path runs in both the eviction and handoff code paths.

oliver: Agree. Current ownership model: lease {owner, epoch, token}. Eviction -> mark demoting, schedule callback via token queue. Handoff -> try steal and schedule cleanup. If steal and eviction both race, both schedule. We need an ordering rule.

sam: Two quick options: (A) centralize callback enqueue behind the lease manager so scheduleCallback(token) is idempotent, or (B) carry a 'cancelled' bit on the token and have enqueue check-and-set. Both are ok but (A) is cleaner for correctness; (B) lower-touch.

maria: Option A sounds good but it's a bit of an API change for the lease manager. If we add `leaseManager.enqueueOnce(token, cbId)` that'll prevent duplicates across subsystems. We should also add a metric for duplicate scheduling: `kvcache.eviction.duplicate_callback.count`.

runtime-bot: deploy/5556667000 succeeded to canary at 2026-02-11T14:50Z :white_check_mark:

nora: Another angle: make the demote callback idempotent at the application layer. If the callback checks an atomic state transition from DEMOTING->DEMOTED and only acts if CAS succeeds, duplicates are harmless. Downsides: more checks inside hot path and risk of masking other logic bugs.

devex: For rollout safety, recommend a three-step plan: 1) add an invariant metric and a debug-only assert (non-fatal) to catch duplicate scheduling in prod for a week; 2) implement leaseManager.enqueueOnce (guarded behind a feature flag); 3) harden the callback with CAS as a last-resort defensive measure.

sam: Sounds solid. Also we should add a short integration test that concurrently races eviction and handoff loops for 1000 iterations in CI to catch regressions. I can add it to eng-runtime/integration/kv_race_tests.

maria: Small implementation note: `enqueueOnce` needs a stable key — use token.id + epoch. If we use token ptr, GC or regeneration will break the de-dup.

oliver: Telemetry keys we want: `kvcache.eviction.duplicate_callback.count`, `kvcache.handoff.steal_vs_eviction_race.count`, `kvcache.demote.callback_cas_fail.count`. Add trace logs at DEBUG with token id/epoch.

nora: One subtle correctness case: if a callback is deduped but one path's cleanup would have advanced epoch (e.g., demote increments epoch) while the other expects old epoch, we must ensure callbacks check current epoch and no-op if stale. That ties back to idempotent checks.

sam: I'll prototype enqueueOnce + epoch check. If we can get a small benchmark showing <1% overhead on demote path we can ship behind feature flag.

maria: I'll add the CI stress test and a short playback of the canary logs to a debug endpoint for easier repro.

oliver: Plan ack. Owners: sam (enqueueOnce + feature flag), maria (CI stress test + debug endpoint), nora (invariant metric & trace schema), devex (rollout checklist). We'll circle back in 48h with results. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
